notes:
Account snapshot:
- Product interest: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for customer-facing personalization and chat; also Evaluate Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
- Capacity ask: initial reserve = 8 x A100-class GPUs (able to scale to 16 in Q3). Throughput target: sustained 1.8k tokens/s across 8 GPUs; burst to 3.5k tokens/s. Latency SLOs: 95th <= 120ms for 512-token prompts, p50 ~ 40-60ms.
- SLA negotiation highlights: customer legal pushing for 99.99% uptime; Redwood standard dedicated SLA currently proposed 99.95%. Customer wants explicit credit schedule tied to monthly uptime and separate credits for latency breach windows.
- Proposed credit schedule (Redwood draft): 99.95-99.99% = 10% service credit, 99.9-99.95% = 25%, <99.9% = 50% (negotiable). Customer counters: wants flatter scale and quicker remediation SLAs.
- Maintenance windows: Redwood proposed monthly 02:00-04:00 PT maintenance with 48h notice; Tectonic requires maintenance outside EMEA peak (they operate global promotions) and requests ability to nominate a 6h blackout period per quarter.
- Support & response times: Discussed P1/P0 escalation paths. Tectonic expects P1 response within 15 minutes and continuous pager until issue resolved; Redwood offered 30-minute phone response for P1 and 2-hour acknowledgement for P2 with follow-ups. SE pushed case studies showing MTTR median 45 mins on dedicated.
- Routing/fallback: They require automatic fallback to a lower-cost model in a different region if capacity constrained; also want commit to cross-region failover time <120s.
- Security/compliance: Must support SSO (SAML), audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, KMS-managed keys in their GCP/VPC, and data residency controls for EU customers. Security team opened SEC-78 requesting encryption-at-rest diagram and HSM integration notes.
- Procurement notes: procurement asked for a clear monthly invoice line for reserved GPUs vs. overage compute and a 12-month vs 24-month pricing comparison. They prefer annual commit.
- POC status: 3-week POC finished 2026-02-28. Results: latency SLOs met in single-region tests, throughput tests hit 92% of target when using recommended batching; Optimize recs reduced token cost by ~18% in test queries.
- Quotes from sponsors:
  - "Need contractual uptime that matches our SLAs to merchants — otherwise we absorb risk." — VP Product
  - "If you can guarantee cross-region failover under two minutes, we can consider a 24-month commit." — Head of Infra
- Action items so far (timeline):
  2026-01-20: Intro call w/ Jordan/Morgan. Quick scoping.
  2026-01-29: Deep-dive technical w/ infra + SE (fireflies ff_20260129_0321). Discussed reserved GPU sizing.
  2026-02-05: Delivered POC plan + test harness (drive link).
  2026-02-28: POC wrap — performance report sent.
  2026-03-02: Legal first pass on SLA (redline requested).
  2026-03-05: Follow-up on credit schedule; Morgan presented alternate credit ladder.
  2026-03-08: Exec alignment call — procurement and VP Product attended (fireflies ff_20260212_0943).
- Current sentiment: cautious but positive. They're price- and risk-sensitive; will pay for stronger guarantees but want clear credit schedule + short remediation times.
- Stated non-negotiables: audit logging + KMS integration + data residency for EU merchants.
- Suggested Redwood negotiation points to push:
  1) Offer 99.95% baseline + optional 99.99% premium tier (additional monthly fee) — include clear test/measurement methodology.
  2) Define credits that cap at 50% of monthly reserved fees and max one payout per incident month.
  3) Offer agreed-upon maintenance windows with the option for one customer-controlled quarterly blackout.
  4) Commit to P1 callback within 30 minutes with dedicated escalation engineer; offer an option for 15-minute SOC-level on-call at higher support tier.
- Next steps (short): legal to review Redwood SLA redline by 2026-03-15; Morgan to produce detailed credit schedule and failover test plan; procurement to confirm preferred billing cadence by 2026-03-20.

Maintenance: monthly 02:00-04:00 PT proposed; customer requests EMEA-safe window + quarterly customer blackout option. Support: P1 30min callback offered, customer asks 15min; propose paid premium for 15min SLA. Credit cap recommendation: max 50% of monthly reserved fees. Failover: target cross-region failover <120s; include runbook and annual DR test in SOW.
